Thank you all for these critical flags. Let me synthesize what I'm hearing and outline how I plan to revise the approval package before Monday.

First, on patent title — Daniel, your recommendation to make closing conditional on Northlake delivering the executed inventor assignment for the continuation application is the cleaner path. I'd prefer that over carving out the continuation, since the business team needs the full platform. We should also consider whether the pre-signing patent diligence requirement in the current draft gives us leverage to demand the assignment be resolved as part of that diligence.

Second, on the existing grant — Martin, we need a carveout in the license for the University Research Consortium's academic research and teaching rights. I'll add that to the draft and make clear to the business team that our exclusivity is subject to that carveout.

Third, on royalty — Sofia, a 3% rate above a validated 225-basis-point ceiling is a material discrepancy. Before I go back to Northlake to renegotiate, I want to ask: is there anything in your benchmark that would justify a premium, or should we push hard to get down to the ceiling?

Fourth, on export controls — Nora, I'll incorporate the prohibition on transfers to military end users and the annual end-use screening certification requirement into the license draft, and add the ECCN 3A001 classification to the transaction checklist.

Given that we have four open issues — title, carveout, royalty, and export controls — I want to assess whether we can still sign next Monday or whether we need to push the timeline. I'd like each of you to confirm: can your respective issues be resolved by Monday with the right deal-term changes, or do any of you recommend delaying signature? That will determine whether I advise the business team to target Monday or request an extension from Northlake.

Thank you all. Based on everyone's input, here is my assessment and plan.

Daniel's title issue is clearly the critical path item. I agree we should not close on an exclusive license with a known title gap on a pending continuation application that may contain claims critical to the platform. I will contact Northlake today to request confirmation on whether they can deliver the executed and recorded inventor assignment by Monday. If they cannot, I will advise the business team to request a signing extension rather than sign with a title defect.

Here is how I plan to proceed on each issue:

1. Patent Title: I will make closing explicitly conditional on Northlake delivering the executed and recorded inventor assignment for the continuation application. I will also leverage the pre-signing patent diligence requirement in the current draft to frame this as a diligence item Northlake must resolve. Daniel, please circulate your title memorandum today so I can attach it to the approval package.

2. University Research Consortium Carveout: Martin, please draft the reserved-rights clause and the business-team note today. I will incorporate the carveout into the license draft and ensure the business team understands their exclusivity is subject to it.

3. Royalty: Sofia, I accept your recommendation. I will push Northlake to renegotiate down to or below the 225-basis-point ceiling. If Northlake or the business team insists on 3%, I will require documented justification and explicit approval at the appropriate level before proceeding. I will not sign at 3% without one or the other.

4. Export Controls: Nora, please provide the specific contract language for the military end-user prohibition and the annual end-use screening certification today. I will incorporate both into the license draft and add the ECCN 3A001 classification to the transaction checklist.

My recommendation to the business team will be: we target Monday only if Northlake confirms the inventor assignment can be delivered and recorded by then, and if the royalty is renegotiated or a documented premium is approved. If either condition is not met, we request an extension. I will not advise signing with the title gap unresolved.

Does anyone have additional concerns before I begin drafting the revised approval package and reaching out to Northlake?
